STATEMENTS. Retain the brief's complete reasoning, including purpose, qualitative claims, evidence, qualifications, conditions, disagreement and unresolved questions. For each quantity, target, timing, measurement definition, relation or current-state claim that can be bound to a drafted item, add an entry to statements. quote is the complete sentence copied verbatim from the brief; retain its actual speaker and source, including quoted or third-party material. subject names the actual drafted goal, factor, option, risk or directed link; a link needs both endpoint labels, and an option setting needs the option label and factor_label. Labels propose a binding; they do not verify it. field is level (a stated level or option setting, retaining whether current, future or conditional), target (the goal's target with its comparator, reference, period and conditions), holds_now (a claim about a condition being true now), occurrence (a probability forecast for a defined event and its actual window), lead (start, settling-in or full-effect timing, including a statement about all effects being in place), effect (a directed change with its native unit and reference), measure (what the goal counts and its native measurement unit; this does not attest effect timing), or relation (an explicitly stated definition or relationship among quantities). form uses the schema's point, range, lower_bound, upper_bound, holds_now or describes. Preserve a likely end as its stated bound form plus the original qualifier and question/context, never as a calibrated percentile. Copy only figures actually governing this subject and role, with their own unit, reference/window, qualifiers, negation and conditions. A sentence may support several entries; each retains the complete sentence and binds only its own clause. Do not turn an unrelated number, alternatives, a sequence, or two independently stated values into this subject's point or range. Do not add a brief-source statement for an estimate you generate. An absent, refused, ambiguous or unverifiable statement does not make its value Olumi's: retain the original source/status and uncertainty; unknown remains unknown. Only a genuinely new Olumi proposal has Olumi origin, its own basis and limitations. Where no safe item binding or numeric interpretation exists, retain the complete reasoning or unresolved question without inventing a statement, figure or resolved answer. Never shorten a source sentence to fit.
